method match_parens(lst: seq<string>) returns (result: string)
    requires |lst| == 2 // The input list must contain exactly two strings
    requires forall i :: 0 <= i < |lst| ==> (lst[i] == "(" || lst[i] == ")") // Each string must consist of only '(' or ')'
    ensures result == "Yes" || result == "No" // The result must be either "Yes" or "No"
    ensures (result == "Yes") ==> (exists order :: order == [lst[0], lst[1]] || order == [lst[1], lst[0]] && is_good(order[0] + order[1])) // If the result is "Yes", there exists an order of concatenation that yields a good string
    ensures (result == "No") ==> (!exists order :: order == [lst[0], lst[1]] || order == [lst[1], lst[0]] && is_good(order[0] + order[1])) // If the result is "No", no order of concatenation can yield a good string

method is_good(s: string) returns (b: bool)
    ensures b ==> (count_open(s) == count_close(s)) // A string is good if the count of '(' and ')' are equal
    ensures !b ==> (count_open(s) != count_close(s) || !is_balanced(s)) // A string is not good if the counts are unequal or if it is not balanced

method count_open(s: string) returns (n: int)
    // Counts the number of '(' in string s

method count_close(s: string) returns (n: int)
    // Counts the number of ')' in string s

method is_balanced(s: string) returns (b: bool)
    // Checks if the parentheses in string s are balanced
```
